record.paper_title: The Status of Polycyclic Group-Based Cryptography: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: For polycyclic groups, determine the computational complexity of the search endomorphism problem and its automorphism variant. In the endomorphism version supported by the source text, the input includes a group S and elements s and t with the promise that t = phi(s) for some endomorphism phi from S to S, and the task is to find such an endomorphism; the automorphism variant asks the analogous question when the map is required to be an automorphism.

evidence.quote: The endomorphism search problem in S should be demonstrably NP-hard.
Alice chooses an endomorphism φ : S → S as her private key. Alice then chooses elements s, t ∈ S such that t = φ(s).
(8) What is the complexity of the search endomorphism (automorphism) prob- lem in polycyclic groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $S$ is called polycyclic if it admits a subnormal series $S = S_0 \triangleright S_1 \triangleright \cdots \triangleright S_n = \{1\}$ in which every quotient $S_i/S_{i+1}$ is cyclic. Such groups are finitely presented and admit effective polycyclic presentations, so elements can be encoded by normal-form words and group operations are computable.

Consider the following two algorithmic problems:

(a) Search Endomorphism Problem in polycyclic groups. Given a finitely presented polycyclic group $S$ (specified by a polycyclic presentation) together with two elements $s, t \in S$, under the promise that there exists a group endomorphism $\varphi : S \to S$ with $\varphi(s) = t$, compute such an endomorphism $\varphi$ (output as the images of the polycyclic generators of $S$).

(b) Search Automorphism Problem in polycyclic groups. The same problem as (a), but with the promise strengthened to: there exists a group automorphism $\varphi : S \to S$ with $\varphi(s) = t$, and the required output $\varphi$ must be an automorphism.

Determine the computational complexity of problems (a) and (b). In particular, decide whether either of these search problems is NP-hard.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open question in the surveys on polycyclic group-based cryptography, and recent literature on algorithmic problems for polycyclic groups (e.g., works on the complexity of the conjugacy search problem in polycyclic and matrix groups) does not report a resolution of the complexity of the (auto)endomorphism search problem in this setting. No source found establishing tight complexity bounds or NP-hardness for the search endomorphism/automorphism problem in polycyclic groups.

status_evidence.title: Complexity of Conjugacy Search in some Polycyclic and Matrix Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work studies conjugacy search complexity in polycyclic groups; does not resolve endomorphism search complexity.
status_evidence.claim: Recent complexity work on polycyclic groups addresses related (conjugacy) problems but not the endomorphism/automorphism search complexity.
